name: Tennessee
notes: Economic nexus first effective October 1, 2019 (Sales Tax Institute, TaxJar "Effective date: October 1, 2019"); Avalara's Effective date cell shows July 1, 2019. effective_date is the date the threshold was lowered to $100,000: Sales Tax Institute "Tennessee lowered their threshold from $500,000 to $100,000, effective October 1, 2020."; Avalara lists the previous rules as "$500,000 in sales only prior to October 1, 2020". Sales Tax Institute's Threshold cell still displays "$500,000*"; the $100,000 figure comes from that footnote, from Avalara's "$100,000 in sales only" and from TaxJar's "Sales exceeding $100,000 in the state in the previous 12 months". Comparator is from TaxJar wording "exceeding"; Sales Tax Institute and Avalara do not state it. Sales measure "Retail sales" is from Sales Tax Institute only; Avalara lists "Sales to customers in the state", "Exempt sales" and "Services (taxable and exempt)" as included without naming a measure. Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales excluded from the threshold for individual sellers effective October 1, 2020"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as excluded and "Marketplace sales included prior to October 1, 2020".

sources.title: State-by-state guide to economic nexus laws

name: Texas
notes: Texas Comptroller Remote Sellers page: "Remote sellers with total Texas revenue of less than $500,000 in the preceding twelve calendar months are not required to obtain a tax permit or collect, report and remit state and local use tax." and "Your total Texas revenue is based on gross revenue from taxable and nontaxable sales of tangible personal property and services into Texas."; also "if you exceed the $500,000 safe harbor amount, you are required to obtain a permit". The official page states no date from which remote sellers had to collect. Sales Tax Institute: "$500,000", Effective Date "October 1, 2019"; Avalara: "$500,000 in sales only", Effective date "July 1, 2019"; TaxJar: "Sales above $500,000 in Texas in the previous calendar year." and "Effective date: October 1, 2019. (The initial timeframe for calculating these revenues was July 1, 2018, through June 30, 2019.)" Effective date is not recorded because the sources differ and the official page states none. Measurement period is the official wording "preceding twelve calendar months", also used by Sales Tax Institute ("Preceding twelve calendar months"); Avalara says "Previous 12-month period"; TaxJar's "previous calendar year" differs and the official page decides. Comparator is not recorded: the official page words the safe harbor both "less than $500,000" and "exceed the $500,000 safe harbor amount", and TaxJar says "above $500,000". Sales measure: Sales Tax Institute "Gross revenue: including taxable, nontaxable, and tax-exempt sales"; Avalara "Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property and services into the state". Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales included towards the threshold for individual sellers"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as included; the official page adds "A remote seller who only sells through a marketplace provider that certifies they are collecting and reporting sales and use tax on the remote seller's behalf is not required to hold a Texas tax permit."

name: Utah
notes: Economic nexus first effective January 1, 2019 (Sales Tax Institute, Avalara, TaxJar). effective_date is the date the transaction threshold was removed: Sales Tax Institute "Utah removed their 200 transactions threshold effective July 1, 2025."; Avalara lists the previous rule as "$100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to July 1, 2025". TaxJar does not mention the removal and still shows "Effective date: January 1, 2019". Comparator is from TaxJar wording "Sales of $100,000 or more in the state in the current or last calendar year."; Sales Tax Institute and Avalara do not state it. Sales measure: Sales Tax Institute "Gross sales"; Avalara "Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property and services into the state". Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales excluded from the threshold for individual sellers"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as excluded.

sources.title: State-by-state guide to economic nexus laws

name: Vermont
notes: Sales Tax Institute: "$100,000 or 200 or more separate transactions"; Avalara: "$100,000 or 200 transactions"; TaxJar: "Sales of $100,000 or more in the state, or at least 200 individual sales transactions into the state during any preceding twelve-month period." Comparator: "or more" and "at least" are stated for both thresholds by TaxJar and for the transaction count by Sales Tax Institute. Measurement period is not recorded because the sources differ in precision: Sales Tax Institute "Prior four calendar quarters"; Avalara "Previous 12-month period". Sales measure "Gross sales" is from Sales Tax Institute only; Avalara lists "Sales of tangible personal property and services into the state" and "Exempt sales" as included without naming a measure. Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales included towards the threshold for individual sellers"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as included. Avalara adds the qualifier "Businesses that only sell tax-exempt items into Vermont are not required to register for sales tax", which the other sources do not mention.

sources.title: State-by-state guide to economic nexus laws

name: Virginia
notes: Virginia Department of Taxation page: "A remote seller or marketplace facilitator has economic nexus if they sell or facilitate the sale of more than $100,000 in annual gross retail sales or 200 or more transactions to Virginia customers."; "A remote seller is any dealer that, in the previous or current calendar year, either receives greater than $100,000 in gross revenue from retail sales, or engages in 200 or more separate retail sales transactions". Comparator is not recorded: the official page words the dollar threshold "more than" and "greater than" but the transaction count "200 or more", and TaxJar words both "or more" and "at least". Sales measure: Sales Tax Institute "Retail sales"; Avalara lists "Sales of tangible personal property" without naming a measure. Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales excluded from the threshold for individual sellers"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as excluded; the official page counts "annual direct sales to Virginia customers (sales that aren't made through the facilitator)". The effective date July 1, 2019 is given by Sales Tax Institute, Avalara and TaxJar; the official page states no date. registration_url is the "Register online" link on the official page.

name: Washington
notes: Sales Tax Institute lists two tiers: "$10,000 or comply with the notice and reporting requirements" (Effective Date "January 1, 2018 for collection or notice and reporting option") and "Gross income of the business exceeding $100,000" (Effective Date "October 1, 2018"), with the footnote "October 1, 2018 through December 31, 2019, sellers with 200 or more separate transactions into Washington must collect. However, effective March 14, 2019 the threshold will only be $100,000. The state removed the 200 transactions threshold." and, for the sales measure, "Effective January 1, 2020 it became a gross income standard." Avalara: "$100,000 in sales only", included "Cumulative gross annual income", previous rules "Cumulative gross receipts from retail sales and taxable services into the state prior to December 31, 2019" and "Cumulative gross annual income as of January 1, 2020". TaxJar: "Sales of $100,000 or more into the state into Washington in the current or last calendar year." and "effective July 1, 2019, SSB Bill 5581 eliminated both the notice and reporting requirements established in the state's 2018 Marketplace Fairness law in addition to the 200 transaction trigger." Comparator and effective_date are not recorded because sources differ. The $10,000 notice-and-reporting tier is not encoded in the threshold fields. Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales included towards the threshold for individual sellers"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as included.

sources.title: State-by-state guide to economic nexus laws

name: West Virginia
notes: Sales Tax Institute: "$100,000 or 200 or more separate transactions"; Avalara: "$100,000 or 200 transactions"; TaxJar: "Sales of $100,000/year in gross revenue the previous calendar year OR 200 or more separate transactions in the previous calendar year." Sales Tax Institute, Avalara and TaxJar all give the effective date "January 1, 2019". Comparator is not recorded: only the transaction count is described with "or more" and the wording of the dollar threshold is not stated. Measurement period is not recorded because sources differ. Sales measure: Sales Tax Institute "Gross sales"; Avalara "Gross sales of tangible personal property and services into the state"; TaxJar "gross revenue". Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales included towards the threshold for individual sellers"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as included.

sources.title: State-by-state guide to economic nexus laws

name: Wisconsin
notes: Economic nexus first effective October 1, 2018 (Sales Tax Institute, Avalara, TaxJar). effective_date is the date the transaction threshold was removed: Sales Tax Institute "Wisconsin removed their 200 transactions threshold, effective February 20, 2021."; Avalara lists the previous rule as "$100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to February 20, 2021"; TaxJar shows "Effective date: October 1, 2018; Updated February 2021". Comparator is from TaxJar wording "Sales of $100,000 or more annually in the previous or current calendar year."; Sales Tax Institute and Avalara do not state it. Sales measure: Sales Tax Institute "Gross sales"; Avalara "Annual gross sales of tangible personal property into the state". Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales included towards the threshold for individual sellers" with the qualifier "but if all sales are made through a marketplace that is collecting, the individual seller is not required to register"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as included and adds "Businesses that make only nontaxable sales into Wisconsin are not required to register for sales tax".

name: Wyoming
notes: Economic nexus first effective February 1, 2019 (Sales Tax Institute, Avalara, TaxJar). effective_date is the date the transaction threshold was removed: Sales Tax Institute "Wyoming removed their 200 transactions threshold, effective July 1, 2024."; Avalara lists the previous rule as "$100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to July 1, 2024"; TaxJar "As of July 1, 2024, Wyoming removed the 200 transaction threshold from their economic nexus requirements." Comparator is from TaxJar wording "Sales of $100,000 or more into the state."; Sales Tax Institute and Avalara do not state it. Sales measure: Sales Tax Institute "Gross sales"; Avalara "Annual gross sales of tangible personal property into the state". Marketplace: Sales Tax Institute "Marketplace sales excluded from the threshold for individual sellers"; Avalara lists "Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator" as excluded.
